gen-dafont-disorder-gf-quando: Disorder's lowercase towers, its glyphs spaced well apart and raw. Quando answers in text serif, widely spaced and tall in the middle, so bump its size up a notch to let it hold its own.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-bree-serif: Dogica stretches its tracking wide, with lowercase nearly as tall as the capitals and every curve left open. And Bree Serif goes literary instead, its oversized small letters doing the quiet, refined work the heading never attempts.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-judson: Industrial pipework meets old-world ink. Existence keeps every stroke at the same mass, and Judson swings from heavy shoulder to thin arc, so the page gets rod stock above and brush-lifted curves below.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-noto-naskh-arabi: Noto Naskh Arabic keeps a very tall x-height and light engraved-brass contrast. Beneath Existence, whose curves turn corners without any pressure swell, a long read moves along smoothly, its mild thick-thin shifts setting the pace.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-noto-serif-armen: Existence looks like bent tubing, with portholes for counters and terminals cut short of the bowl. Noto Serif Armenian has big open counters and a mild stroke contrast, though shrinking the heading would waste that tubular punch.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-noto-serif-grant: Pure machined heft, with crossbars as thick as the stems. Noto Serif Grantha softens that with slightly thinner hairlines and oversized small letters, a tempered contrast that never jolts.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-noto-serif-khojk: Existence holds one line width through curves and straights alike. Noto Serif Khojki adds a faint swelling in each rounded letter, with short ascenders above big bowls, and that softness is the pair's best asset.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-noto-serif-makas: Noto Serif Makasar has a soft step from heavy to light and a towering x-height, like a stubby carpenter's pencil. Existence keeps every stroke at one gauge, and a slightly larger Makasar would help hold its own against it.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-noto-serif-oriya: Noto Serif Oriya reads dignified and authoritative, its curves a touch heavier than the joins and its lowercase close to cap height. Existence is best at rod-stock strokes of identical thickness, while Noto Serif Oriya does its best with a soft shift between fat and slim.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-noto-serif-tibet: Existence builds arms and legs of constant width, industrial and modern. Noto Serif Tibetan follows with a thickness shift you feel more than see, so Existence earns its keep when big and brief.
